runs.title: Jolie–Pitt winery case settled: the details
runs.prompt: On 25 November 2026, Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt reportedly settled their long-running legal fight over the Château Miraval French winery, a case that had aired abuse allegations. Find out the actual substance of the settlement: what was the dispute about, did a settlement get announced, and are there any terms or statements? Prefer a source that is NOT paywalled. Good starting points are the AP News article and The Guardian, both of which covered the story.
runs.answer: Yes — a settlement was announced on 25 Nov 2026, but with no disclosed terms: in a joint statement their representatives said "We have settled out of court in the best interests of our family and will not be commenting further," and added that any quotes in media stories attributed to "sources" were not coming from either of them or anyone close to them. Both sides moved to dismiss their claims against each other, and the terms of the agreement were not made public. The dispute: the couple bought a controlling interest in Château Miraval in 2008 and married there in 2014; after Jolie filed for divorce in 2016 (they were declared legally single in 2019, divorce finalized in 2024), she sold her stake in the winery to the Stoli Group, a spirits maker controlled by Yuri Shefler, for $164m in 2021. Pitt sued her in February 2022, saying she broke their agreement not to sell their interests without the other's consent. In her October 2022 counter-suit Jolie alleged abusive behavior leading to the divorce, saying talks to sell her share to Pitt collapsed over his demand that she sign an NDA barring her from speaking about "Pitt's physical and emotional abuse of her and their children"; Pi

runs.title: Hera's asteroid-crater photos: the numbers
runs.prompt: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has returned close-up images of the stadium-sized crater left on the asteroid Dimorphos after NASA's DART spacecraft deliberately slammed into it. Find out the key facts: how big is the crater, where exactly is it, and which asteroid was struck? Give figures where you can, from an accessible source such as ESA's news page or the BBC.
runs.answer: Partial result: NASA's DART struck Dimorphos, the small moon of the near-Earth asteroid Didymos (65803), on 26 September 2022, and ESA's Hera — which reached the binary system in November 2026 — imaged the resulting crater, described as "stadium-sized" and "almost as large as the body itself," i.e. comparable to Dimorphos's ~150 m mean diameter (177 × 174 × 116 m). Dimorphos's orbit around Didymos was shortened by about 33 minutes by the impact. I could not verify an exact crater diameter/depth figure or its precise position on Dimorphos: the supplied BBC URL (bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw1561435gwo) returns a hard 404, and ESA's long article was truncated on every route I tried (direct, Wayback Machine, text proxy which returned 401), with search engines bot-walled or returning no usable snippet.

runs.title: Tesla's EU self-driving vote: why postponed
runs.prompt: The European Union has postponed a planned discussion or vote on approving Tesla's 'Full Self-Driving' (FSD) self-driving technology. Find out what happened: to what new date was the vote pushed, and why was it postponed? Cite specifics and a readable source such as Electrek or CNBC (not a paywall).
runs.answer: The EU's Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles (TCMV) meeting to consider — and potentially vote on — bloc-wide approval of Tesla's system (now sold in Europe as "Tesla Assisted Driving," renamed from Full Self-Driving) was pushed from its originally scheduled December 1, 2026 date to December 15, 2026, per a European Commission spokesperson who confirmed the new date to Reuters. No official reason was given: Electrek states plainly that "nobody has given a reason for the change," and both outlets frame the slip as the latest in a long series of missed European dates rather than a Tesla-specific problem — the committee had already discussed the file twice without voting, and the Dec. 15 meeting is still only a discussion that could be deferred into 2027. Note that Belgium's Flanders transport ministry initially said the meeting moved to December 7 before the Commission clarified December 15. Context: EU-wide approval needs at least 15 of 27 member states representing 65% of the population; 12 countries have recognized the Dutch (RDW) April 10 approval, and a rejection at EU level would invalidate those national approvals.

runs.title: Big Ten volleyball: who's left for the title?
runs.prompt: The inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament is down to four teams, with Nebraska, Penn State, Wisconsin and Purdue reportedly still in contention. Find out which four teams remain, when the next matches (semifinal or final) are played, and what channel or platform is showing them. Start with the Big Ten's own news pages.
runs.answer: The four semifinalists at the inaugural Allstate Big Ten Volleyball Tournament were No. 1 Nebraska, No. 2 Penn State, No. 3 Wisconsin and No. 5 Purdue. The semifinals were played Tuesday, Nov. 24 at Fishers Event Center in Fishers, Ind. — Nebraska vs. Purdue at 6 p.m. ET and Penn State vs. Wisconsin at 8 p.m. ET — both televised on Big Ten Network (also streamable on FOX One). Nebraska beat Purdue 3-1 and Wisconsin beat Penn State 3-1, so the championship match is Wednesday, Nov. 25 at 8 p.m. ET, Nebraska vs. Wisconsin, airing live on FOX (the first broadcast network to carry a women's college volleyball conference tournament final).
